newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa producers initiate new maize scheme talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa producers initiate new maize scheme talks.

text.p: South Africa's National Maize Producers Organisation (Nampo) has begun drawing up marketing rules for the new maize season starting in May next year.

But the scheme, expected to be a move closer to a free market, will not be in place for several months leaving farmers who begin planting their crops this month without clear direction for production decisions.
"It is extremely important for maize farmers that we have clarification on what the future holds for them," said Giel van Zyl, general manager of Nampo.
"We have taken the initiative in that regard...but it is impossible to have it in place before planting."

South Africa's maize industry is grappling with greater deregulation, which this year saw the export market opened to private traders for the first time following government withdrawal from the domestic market last year.
The government, via the state-owned Maize Board, is still active in the export market.

Nampo had already held discussions with a number of parties, including co-operatives and millers, and would submit proposals on the new scheme to the Maize Advisory Committee, which represents a cross-section of maize industry players.
"That will be probably (be) early in November," van Zyl told Reuters.
From Nampo's discussions so far, Van Zyl said the 1997/98 marketing year was likely to see further moves towards market liberalisation.

"Invariably it is moving closer and closer to a total free market. But there seems to be some consensus...that we must be careful not to end up with producer prices that will make maize production unprofitable."
But industry players were divided on the need for continued government intervention in the maize market, he said.
"Nampo sees a role for an implementation body, that's what the new (Marketing of Agricultural Products) Act stipulates. But all the role players do not necessarily agree."
Derek Hanekom, the Minister of Agriculture, has repeatedly committed himself to creating freer agricultural markets. He has said market forces should be the strongest determinant.

Hanekom earlier this year urged speed on drawing up a maize scheme for the 1997/98 season in a bid to prevent a repeat of the discord seen this year when some players tried to change the rules midway through the season.

In August he said, "...I will be requesting the Maize Advisory Committee to urgently submit to the National Marketing Council any consensus position it may have on the type of intervention necessary for the 1997/98 marketing year."
Peet Wessels, chairman of the MAC and National Marketing Council said there had been no objections to Nampo spearheading the talks.
"The other role players in the MAC did not object, in fact they thought it was a good idea," Wessels said.
South Africa expects a bumper maize crop of 9.484 million tonnes this season, up from 4.406 million in 1995, following soaking rains. --Johannesburg newsroom +27-11 482 1003
